clue.text: Title to property that's in the outskirts of London

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here within the city's edges
outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of the city name

parts.note: that's means 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A deed for a house somewhere in suburban London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outskirts of' London gives L and N, the first and last letters; 'in' puts IE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right or claim over property held as security for a debt.

clue.text: Combine 7 or 29, 8 or 21 Across, 18 or 22, comprehensively

parts.note: the answers to 7 Down (a piece of hair) and 29 Across (a ringlet) are both a lock of hair
repute and reserve are both senses of stock (standing; a store)
the little word and is the one that combines things in a list
a keg is a barrel, and to barrel along is to speed

explanation.surface: An instruction to merge several cross-referenced answers in their entirety.
explanation.walkthrough: Each pair of cross-references points to two answers that share one synonym: LOCK, STOCK and BARREL; 'Combine' supplies the joining AND. The answer runs on into 17 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'lock, stock and barrel' means completely, every part of a gun included.

clue.text: Leaderless guys in revolutionary movement joining up…

indicators.note: without its leader, the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: guys are men
rolling is movement by turning over and over, as a revolving wheel does

explanation.surface: Men without a leader are signing up to an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics, but it describes turning motion. 'Leaderless' takes M from MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolling is signing on as a member, which is joining up.

clue.text: Combine 19 Across or 20, 1 Across or 9, 12 or 25, comprehensively

parts.note: disappeared and exited both mean left, as in went away
a title or lien is a right, and correctly means rightly or right
the little word and is the one that combines things in a list
a nucleus and a core are both the centre of something

explanation.surface: An instruction to merge several cross-referenced answers in their entirety.
explanation.walkthrough: Each pair of cross-references points to two answers that share one synonym: LEFT, RIGHT and CENTRE; 'Combine' supplies the joining AND. The answer runs on into 28 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'left, right and centre' means everywhere, in every direction, thoroughly.

clue.text: … and others coming up behind

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: et al. is Latin shorthand for 'and others'

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: further recruits trail in at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 2 Down but does nothing in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Late and behind both describe being overdue or after schedule.

clue.text: Arrive by air and take carriage home

parts.note: a fly was a light horse-drawn hired carriage
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: Land at the airport and grab a taxi back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly is an old one-horse hackney carriage, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly in is to come to a place by plane.

clue.text: Character in Genesis and later book

definitions.meaning: the wife of Isaac in the Old Testament's first book
Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel of that title, much later than Genesis

explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is Isaac's wife in Genesis and also the title of du Maurier's famous novel.

clue.text: Info about style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Some information concerning fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a type or style of artistic work.

clue.text: Piece of hair cut first in anxiety

indicators.note: cut first means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: stress is anxiety

explanation.surface: A lock snipped off during a moment of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of a person's hair.

clue.text: Fame of Peter spread around university

indicators.note: around means the shuffled name goes round the abbreviation
spread here means the letters of the name are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Peter's celebrity spreading across the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges PETER into REPTE; 'around' puts it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is reputation, the standing or renown a person has.

clue.text: Chapter left in rectory amended appropriately

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the combined letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Church records amended as needed at the vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only says C and L join RECTORY; 'amended' rearranges all nine letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: Correctly and appropriately both mean in the proper or fitting way.

clue.text: It's being drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the word reels about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on a spell of heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges BEING; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of heavy drinking, a spell of being drunk.

clue.text: Disposed of possessions, antique included, to eat

indicators.note: included means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper or take food
antique means old

explanation.surface: Someone sold off their antiques just to afford meals.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell up is to sell all one's property or business.

clue.text: Paper rebuffed about strange clue for "heart"

indicators.note: about means the reversed paper goes round the shuffled letters
rebuffed suggests being turned back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: strange means the letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper turned down a weird crossword clue for the word 'heart'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' is the Sun, a British tabloid. 'rebuffed' reverses it, 'strange' jumbles CLUE, and 'about' wraps the first round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core of something, its heart.

clue.text: Poetry's oddness oddly obvious

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: The strangeness of verse is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Take letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of 'oddness'. 'obvious' says the pick is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so they stand for poetry.

clue.text: Legal observations I cited to bar incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly means the letters are set out wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer misquotes comments to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' rearranges the eleven letters of I CITED TO BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter dicta are a judge's passing remarks in a judgment, not binding as precedent.

clue.text: Headgear?

parts.note: read 'head' as a promontory of land jutting into the sea, rather than something worn on top of a person

explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a headland jutting into the sea, and also a garment.

clue.text: Stole dangerous reptile

definitions.meaning: a stole is a long scarf of fur or feathers worn round the neck
a constrictor snake that can crush its prey

explanation.definitionFit: A boa is both a feather scarf and a large constricting snake.

clue.text: Lover accepts command in memo

indicators.note: accepts means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A sweetheart takes instructions by note.
explanation.definitionFit: A bordereau is a memorandum or itemised note, especially in insurance.

clue.text: See 1
Beer like Guinness? Just a little

indicators.note: just a little of the phrase is taken, a short run of letters spanning the words

explanation.surface: Asking whether a drink like Guinness is wanted, only a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just a little' takes a short run from 'liKE Guinness'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keg is beer served from a pressurised cask.

clue.text: Badly appraised by editor, withdrew

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together in a poor, jumbled way

explanation.surface: A writer poorly reviewed by an editor pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges APPRAISED into DISAPPEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappeared and withdrew both mean went away or left.

clue.text: Get madly enraged?

indicators.note: madly means the letters go wild, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone becomes furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges ENRAGED; the whole clue also hints at the answer's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to drive mad or throw into disorder.

clue.text: Went hot, not cold

indicators.note: not means the letter for the second word is left out

parts.note: hot can mean excited or worked up
C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps

explanation.surface: A temperature change from cold to hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes C from EXCITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Exited and went both mean departed.

clue.text: Not first choice for book

definitions.meaning: a substitute or second choice player
to book is to ... in advance

explanation.definitionFit: A reserve is a stand-in, and to reserve is to book a place.

clue.text: Religious follower elevating an emperor

indicators.note: elevating in a down clue means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tsar was an emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: A devotee puts an emperor on a pedestal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rastafarian movement venerates Emperor Haile Selassie, so the surface fits; 'elevating' turns A TSAR upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is a follower of Rastafarianism.

clue.text: On which some can get high rate

definitions.text: On which some can get high
definitions.meaning: an amphetamine drug that gives users a high

explanation.definitionFit: Speed is slang for amphetamine, which people take to get high, and it is also a rate of motion.

clue.text: Rebuilt to be a WWII warship

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together again in another order

explanation.surface: A vessel reconstructed to serve as a wartime warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilt' rearranges TO BE A.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a German fast motor torpedo boat used in the Second World War.

clue.text: American agents getting people back into theatre

indicators.note: into means the reversed people go inside the agents

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: US spies bringing their staff back into the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' here means a film theatre. 'back' reverses the people, and 'into' sets them inside the agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema is a theatre for showing films, a picture theatre.

clue.text: Middle C or other note

parts.note: C, a musical note, taken as written
E is another musical note

explanation.surface: Asking about middle C or some different note on a keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle C' reads as one musical term, but 'Middle' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of something is its middle or central part.

clue.text: Hardback?

parts.note: split the word into 'hard' and 'back': a severe manner, and the rear of a ship, rather than a bound book

explanation.definitionFit: Stern means harsh or severe, and the stern is the back of a ship.

clue.text: Where person's boxed, ignominiously out thus

definitions.meaning: a box on the ears is a cuff to the side of the head
thrown out in disgrace, the idiom for a humiliating dismissal

explanation.definitionFit: One is boxed on the ear when struck there, and someone thrown out shamefully is out on their ear.

clue.text: See 3
Writhe in dog

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Writhe in dog' (4): CUR supplies three letters but no word gives the final L, so a word looks lost in OCR.
